findings: Theorem 1 (l.1381-1392) is imprecise in the zero space E = 0: V = W = {0} satisfies every printed hypothesis, I(V,W) and III(V,W), but not II(V,W), since there is no open half-space (Benzecri.reunion_convexes_dimZero). The same degenerate case as Prop. 8 (l.1323, OQ-165 (d)); Theorem 1 holds in full for E ≠ 0, and in every E when V ≠ W.

III (l.1389-1391) needs « demi-espace H de L » to admit H = L: when V is a point (e.g. the vertex (0,0) of the square, which has I by sommet_carre_proprietes), its support L is a point and has no proper half-space (Benzecri.sommet_carre_sans_demiEspace), so I => III fails under the strict reading. The printed parenthesis « H ∩ W peut être égal à L ∩ W » covers it only if H = L is admitted; for dim L ≥ 1 a proper closed half-space containing the compact L ∩ W exists, so the reading matters only for dim L = 0.

Not a defect, a strengthening: I <-> III needs neither compactness of W nor finite dimension. I => III holds for W convex and V closed non-empty in any real topological vector space (Prop. 7's strong form exists_separe_fort applied in L ∩ W; Benzecri.proprieteIII_of_proprieteI), and III => I needs no topology (Benzecri.proprieteI_of_proprieteIIIlarge).
questions: « un demi-espace H de L » (l.1390): I read it as « a closed half-space of L, or L itself » (the parenthesis « éventuellement, H ∩ W peut être égal à L ∩ W » read as admitting the degenerate half-space H = L). Under the strict reading (proper half-spaces only) the theorem fails for V a point. Open versus closed is NOT immaterial: with open half-spaces only, I => III fails (W = [0,1], V = [0,1/2]: V is compact and I holds, but V is the trace of no open half-line); it is the closed reading, or the wide one (ProprieteIIIlarge, open or closed, degenerate admitted), that makes I => III hold. III => I holds under every reading.
E ≠ 0 (OQ-165 (d), carried over from Prop. 8): read as implicit; formalized with [Nontrivial E], with the E = 0 witness beside it.
